title: The arithmetic-hierarchy definition gives the existential prefix the wrong terminal quantifier.
details:
[Marks, *Computability theory*](https://math.berkeley.edu/~marks/notes/computability_notes_v1.pdf),
2024-02-25, Definition 16.1, p. 67 (PDF p. 67).
Type: invalid definition.

The Sigma prefix starts existentially, but its terminal-quantifier instruction
uses the parity appropriate to a Pi prefix. At `n=4` this gives `∃∀∃∃`
instead of `∃∀∃∀`, changing the specified class.

**Repair and corpus disposition:** for Sigma, use an existential terminal
quantifier at odd levels and a universal one at even levels; reverse this for Pi.
Also correct the matrix arity from `k+m` to `k+n`. Both details were checked
against the rendered page. The arithmetical-hierarchy entry uses the corrected parity and matrix arity in its alternating-prefixes definition.
